title: Theater History and Drama
text: Theater — the performance of drama before an audience — originated in ancient Greece as part of religious festivals honoring Dionysus. Greek theater produced comedy (Aristophanes) and tragedy (Aeschylus, Sophocles, Euripides). Roman theater adapted Greek forms. Medieval theater was largely religious (mystery plays, miracle plays). The Elizabethan era produced Shakespeare and Christopher Marlowe, performing in outdoor theaters like the Globe. Opera developed in Italy around 1600. Modern theater movements include realism (Ibsen, Chekhov), expressionism, absurdism (Beckett's Waiting for Godot), and Brecht's epic theater. Broadway and London's West End are the main centers of commercial theater today.
